text: Statebound checks trading workflows before execution. This is a synthetic fixture, with a twenty USDT spending mandate and zero fees. The example plan is deliberately vulnerable. No real orders are placed.
Find a failure runs a fresh bounded search. The checker finds a path that spends thirty USDT against the twenty USDT mandate. These events come from the plan and fault model.
The first order filled, but its reply was lost. The agent sees a timeout. A stale balance cannot prove failure. Fifteen USDT remains exposed, so a fresh purchase is not free budget.

This is a recorded repair authored by the development Codex session. It queries the original attempt before buying the remaining goal. We validate that candidate and recheck it now. The mandate stays unchanged.

The recoverable replay runs through the shared interpreter and a persistent SQLite ledger. When the order query confirms the fill, the acquisition goal completes. The original ambiguous attempt is never sent again.
Now the lookup stays inconclusive. Statebound finishes unresolved and preserves the reservation. No violation within a finite bound does not mean the environment must let every task complete.

The integration panel shows a genuine recorded public testnet read through the official Binance CLI. Trading remains unavailable. Exported evidence includes the plan, bounds, observations and replay. A separate verifier recomputes the result without an LLM.
